certificate_findings: Application is signed with a code signing certificate

Application is signed with v1 signature scheme, making it vulnerable to Janus vulnerability on Android 5.0-8.0, if signed only with v1 signature scheme. Applications running on Android 5.0-7.0 signed with v1, and v2/v3 scheme is also vulnerable.
Application is signed with SHA1withRSA. SHA1 hash algorithm is known to have collision issues. The manifest file indicates SHA256withRSA is in use.
Certificate algorithm might be vulnerable to hash collision

manifest_findings.title: Activity (com.google.android.gms.tagmanager.TagManagerPreviewActivity) is vulnerable to StrandHogg 2.0
manifest_findings.description: Activity is found to be vulnerable to StrandHogg 2.0 task hijacking vulnerability. When vulnerable, it is possible for other applications to place a malicious activity on top of the activity stack of the vulnerable application. This makes the application an easy target for phishing attacks. The vulnerability can be remediated by setting the launch mode attribute to "singleInstance" and by setting an empty taskAffinity (taskAffinity=""). You can also update the target SDK version (26) of the app to 29 or higher to fix this issue at platform level.
manifest_findings.name: Activity (com.google.android.gms.tagmanager.TagManagerPreviewActivity) is vulnerable to StrandHogg 2.0

pie.description: The shared object is build with -fPIC flag which enables Position independent code. This makes Return Oriented Programming (ROP) attacks much more difficult to execute reliably.

stack_canary.description: This binary has a stack canary value added to the stack so that it will be overwritten by a stack buffer that overflows the return address. This allows detection of overflows by verifying the integrity of the canary before function return.

relocation_readonly.description: This shared object has full RELRO enabled. RELRO ensures that the GOT cannot be overwritten in vulnerable ELF binaries. In Full RELRO, the entire GOT (.got and .got.plt both) is marked as read-only.

metadata.cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File
metadata.description: The App logs information. Sensitive information should never be logged.

metadata.cwe: CWE-749: Exposed Dangerous Method or Function
metadata.description: Insecure WebView Implementation. Execution of user controlled code in WebView is a critical Security Hole.
This App uses SSL certificate pinning to detect or  prevent MITM attacks in secure communication channel.

metadata.cwe: CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')
metadata.description: App uses SQLite Database and execute raw SQL query. Untrusted user input in raw SQL queries can cause SQL Injection. Also sensitive information should be encrypted and written to the database.
App can write to App Directory. Sensitive Information should be encrypted.

metadata.cwe: CWE-312: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information
metadata.description: Files may contain hardcoded sensitive information like usernames, passwords, keys etc.

metadata.cwe: CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
metadata.description: MD5 is a weak hash known to have hash collisions.

metadata.cwe: CWE-330: Use of Insufficiently Random Values
metadata.description: The App uses an insecure Random Number Generator.

playstore_details.title: Kleine Zeitung
playstore_details.description:
The Kleine Zeitung app offers news, background information and opinions on relevant trends and occurrences in your region, Austria and the world.

Select one of 18 regions in Styria or Carinthia to receive all current occurrences in your region - you will never miss a news from home again. Define your personal interests in order to access a your favorite topics and always keep track of things.

The Kleine Zeitung app can be used for operating systems from version 4.4.

Some of the content in the new Kleine Zeitung app is only available with a digital or smartphone subscription. An in-app purchase is possible.

SMARTPHONE SUBSCRIPTION
Those with a smartphone subscription can read all of the content in the app. The price per month for the smartphone subscription is EUR 2.99.

The subscription is automatically renewed if you do not deactivate the automatic subscription renewal at least 24 hours before the end of the term. You can do this in your Google Play settings (Google Play Store - Menu - Account - Subscriptions - Cancel subscription).

Kleine Zeitung clearly states the following information regarding the smartphone subscription:
- Subscription: smartphone
- Duration: monthly subscription
- Price: € 2.99 per month
- Payment is made in the Google Play Store and will be invoiced when the purchase is confirmed.
- The current monthly contributions are paid in advance. The amount will be billed 24 hours before the end of the current term.
- The subscription is automatically renewed. The subscription must be canceled at least 24 hours before the start of the next term in the smartphone settings: Google Play Store - Menu - Account - Subscriptions - Cancel subscription.
- Unused services of a free test phase expire as soon as the user buys a subscription.

By downloading the app, the user accepts the valid general terms of use: http://www.kleinezeitung.at/anb
Data protection regulations: http://www.kleinezeitung.at/datenschutz

If you have any feedback, questions or suggestions, please send them to us at any time to feedback@kleinezeitung.at.

hotspot.title: Found 3 critical permission(s)
hotspot.description:
Ensure that these permissions are required by the application.

android.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION (dangerous): fine (GPS) location - Access fine location sources, such as the Global Positioning System on the phone, where available. Malicious applications can use this to determine where you are and may consume additional battery power.

android.permission.SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW (dangerous): display system-level alerts - Allows an application to show system-alert windows. Malicious applications can take over the entire screen of the phone.

android.permission.READ_PHONE_STATE (dangerous): read phone state and identity - Allows the application to access the phone features of the device. An application with this permission can determine the phone number and serial number of this phone, whether a call is active, the number that call is connected to and so on.
